title: DC and AC Component Separator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: DC component
AC component
DC offset
coupling capacitor
RMS value
AC signals
electrical engineering
description: Interactive MicroSim that separates a composite signal v(t) = VDC + Vm sin(2*pi*f*t) into its DC component (the average value) and its AC component (the oscillation around the average) on three stacked plots with a shared voltage scale, and reports the DC value, AC RMS and total RMS.

learningObjectives: Classify signal components as DC or AC by observing how a composite signal can be separated into its constant and varying parts

controls.label: Component Labels
controls.description: Show or hide the average line and annotations

assumptions: The AC component is a single sinusoid
The coupling capacitor and averaging stage are ideal

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict which plot each slider changes, then observe
keyQuestions: Which plot changes when only the DC offset changes?
What is the average value of the AC component?
Why does a coupling capacitor remove the DC offset but not the oscillation?
commonMisconceptions: A signal that never goes negative has no AC component
Total RMS is the sum of the DC value and the AC RMS value
assessmentOpportunities: Identify the DC component, AC amplitude, AC RMS and total RMS of a given composite signal
